{"step_index":1787,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-11-11T03:07:29Z","input_tokens":2609,"cache_read_tokens":93087,"output_tokens":2305,"content":"# MODULE 9 â€” STATISTICS & LIVE COUNTERS\n## Phase 1: Requirements Analysis and Implementation Planning Summary\n\nWe have completed the comprehensive codebase inspection and architectural planning for **Module 9 of 12: Statistics & Live Counters**.\n\nBoth the plan artifact and workspace plan have been generated:\n- **Artifact:** [`module9_implementation_plan.md`](file:///C:/Users/ACHYUTHA/.gemini/antigravity/brain/62506f25-2248-471f-a539-b379d2a489b9/module9_implementation_plan.md)\n- **Workspace File:** [`dpm101-chatbot/module9_implementation_plan.md`](file:///c:/Users/ACHYUTHA/OneDrive/Desktop/API%20M&H%20Dashboard/dpm101-chatbot/module9_implementation_plan.md)\n\n---\n\n### 1. Original Module 9 Requirements Identified\n\nFrom the original Architecture Specification (`implementation_plan.md` Â§Â§9, 12, 15) and Roadmap:\n1. **Thread-Safe In-Process Counters**: A dedicated service (`backend/services/stats_service.py`) using `threading.Lock` to maintain live runtime counters across the worker's thread pool.\n2. **`GET /api/stats` Endpoint**: An unauthenticated, read-only operational endpoint returning:\n   - `total_requests`: Cumulative chat requests received.\n   - `cache_hits`: Queries served from SQLite cache.\n   - `gemini_calls`: Generations performed via Google Gemini API.\n   - `errors`: Failed requests or unhandled exceptions.\n   - `uptime_seconds`: Elapsed time in seconds since worker boot.\n   - `worker_note`: Explicit disclaimer clarifying single-worker scope and restart data loss:  \n     `\"Counters reflect the current worker process only. Reset on restart.\"`\n3. **Zero Gemini Quota Consumption**: Fetching statistics must never trigger Gemini API calls or consume LLM quota.\n4. **Single-Worker Alignment**: In-process counters align with the single Gunicorn worker architecture (`--workers 1 --threads 2`), avoiding multi-process drift without requiring external distributed infrastructure (e.g., Redis).\n5. **Render Ephemeral Container Disclosure**: Acknowledges that server restarts or redeployments reset in-process counters to zero.\n\n---\n\n### 2. Current vs. Missing Capabilities Analysis\n\n| Capability | Current State in Codebase | Gap / Required for Module 9 |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Persistent SQLite Data** | `conversations` (status, timestamps), `messages` (roles, timestamps), and `query_cache` (access counts, expiration) exist. | Need a unified, single-pass query to aggregate counts across all 3 tables simultaneously. |\n| **Runtime Metrics** | `CacheService` tracks local `_hits` and `_misses`; `RateLimiter` tracks window timestamps. | No central coordinator for `total_requests`, `gemini_calls`, `errors`, `rate_limited_count`, `duplicate_requests_count`, or latency. |\n| **Uptime Tracking** | Process start timestamp is not recorded. | Need monotonic/wall-clock boot timestamp to compute `uptime_seconds`. |\n| **API Endpoints** | `/health` (liveness) and `/api/v1/cache/stats` (cache table details) exist. | `GET /api/stats` and `GET /api/v1/stats` are missing. |\n| **Instrumentation** | `chat_routes.py` and `policy_service.py` execute without incrementing shared metrics. | Need lightweight hooks to record requests, cache hits/misses, AI calls, duplicates, rate-limits, and response latency. |\n| **Frontend UI** | `frontend/index.html` is an empty placeholder. | Need a live stats dashboard card / status bar with passive polling. |\n\n---\n\n### 3. Proposed Architecture & Key Design Decisions\n\n#### A. Central `StatsService` (`backend/services/stats_service.py`)\n- **Mutual Exclusion**: Uses an instance-level `threading.Lock` to synchronize all counter increments and snapshot reads, preventing race conditions or lost updates under concurrent multi-threaded requests.\n- **Latency Sampling**: Tracks cumulative response time and sample count to compute `average_latency_ms`.\n- **Fault-Tolerant Fallback**: If SQLite is locked or unavailable, returns `{\"status\": \"unavailable\"}` for the database section while reliably returning all in-process counters.\n\n#### B. Single-Pass High-Efficiency Database Aggregation\nTo prevent SQLite read contention with active chat writes, all persistent counts are gathered in a single scalar subquery executed under autocommit mode (`isolation_level=None`) with WAL concurrency:\n```sql\nSELECT\n    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM conversations) AS total_conversations,\n    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM conversations WHERE status = 'active') AS active_conversations,\n    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM conversations WHERE status = 'deleted') AS deleted_conversations,\n    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages) AS total_messages,\n    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages WHERE role = 'user') AS user_messages,\n    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages WHERE role = 'assistant') AS assistant_messages,\n    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM query_cache) AS total_cache_entries,\n    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM query_cache WHERE expires_at > datetime('now')) AS active_cache_entries,\n    (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(access_count), 0) FROM query_cache) AS total_cache_accesses;\n```\n*Execution characteristics:* Executes in $< 1\\,\\text{ms}$, transfers a single 9-element tuple, and never loads individual message or conversation rows into Python memory.\n\n#### C. API Endpoint Contract (`GET /api/stats` & `GET /api/v1/stats`)\n```json\n{\n  \"status\": \"ok\",\n  \"uptime_seconds\": 7240,\n  \"total_requests\": 847,\n  \"cache_hits\": 503,\n  \"cache_misses\": 344,\n  \"cache_hit_rate\": 0.5939,\n  \"gemini_calls\": 344,\n  \"errors\": 12,\n  \"rate_limited_count\": 5,\n  \"duplicate_requests_count\": 8,\n  \"average_latency_ms\": 312.45,\n  \"database\": {\n    \"status\": \"connected\",\n    \"total_conversations\": 45,\n    \"active_conversations\": 42,\n    \"deleted_conversations\": 3,\n    \"total_messages\": 120,\n    \"user_messages\": 60,\n    \"assistant_messages\": 60,\n    \"total_cache_entries\": 35,\n    \"active_cache_entries\": 35,\n    \"total_cache_accesses\": 503\n  },\n  \"worker_note\": \"Counters reflect the current worker process only. Reset on restart.\"\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n### 4. Files Expected to Change / Be Created (Phase 2)\n\n| Action | Path | Purpose |\n|---|---|---|\n| **CREATE** | `backend/services/stats_service.py` | Thread-safe `StatsService`, atomic counter locks, uptime, single-pass SQLite aggregation. |\n| **CREATE** | `backend/routes/stats_routes.py` | Blueprint for `GET /api/stats` and `GET /api/v1/stats`. |\n| **MODIFY** | `app.py` | Register `stats_bp` and configure `app.extensions[\"stats_service\"]`. |\n| **MODIFY** | `backend/routes/chat_routes.py` | Hook request arrival, rate-limit rejection, duplicate replay, and latency recording. |\n| **MODIFY** | `backend/services/policy_service.py` | Hook cache hits, cache misses, and Gemini API calls into `stats_service`. |\n| **CREATE** | `tests/test_stats_service.py` | 15+ comprehensive unit, concurrency (20 threads), database, and endpoint integration tests. |\n| **MODIFY** | `README.md` | Document Module 9 completion and API specifications. |\n\n---\n\n### 5. Architectural Integrity & Safety Guarantees\n\n1. **NO Source Code Modified**: Strictly planning analysis was conducted; no Python files were altered.\n2. **NO Database Schema Migrations**: Zero changes to SQLite schema; uses read-only scalar aggregation on existing tables.\n3. **NO External Infrastructure**: Pure Python standard library (`threading`, `time`, `sqlite3`).\n4. **Baseline Regression Preserved**: Current test baseline remains **293 / 293 tests passing in 13.00s**.\n\n---\n\n### Waiting for Your Approval\n\nPlease review the plan in [`module9_implementation_plan.md`](file:///c:/Users/ACHYUTHA/OneDrive/Desktop/API%20M&H Dashboard/dpm101-chatbot/module9_implementation_plan.md). Once approved, we will proceed immediately to **Phase 2: Implementation**.","thinking":"The Python source files haven't been modified during this analysis; only the markdown implementation plan was created. Executive Summary & Exact Traceability\n\nModule 9 implements **Statistics & Live Counters** to provide operational visibility into chatbot throughput, cache effectiveness, AI invocation volume, errors, and worker uptime.\n\n### Traceability to Original Specification\nEvery aspect of this plan is directly derived from the approved project architecture (`implementation_plan.md`):\n\n| Architecture Reference | Requirement Specification | Planned Implementation | Acceptance Verification |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **Roadmap Â§15 (Module 9)** | `stats_service.py` â€” thread-safe in-process counters (`threading.Lock`); no distributed brokers (e.g. Redis) introduced. | Worker lifecycle documentation and single-process scope verification. |\n| **Persistence Limitations Â§12.3** | Render's ephemeral filesystem wipes on restart; in-process stats reset to zero on worker restart. | Documented restart behavior; uptime measured from process start timestamp. | Service initialization test verifies counters start at zero. |\n| **Zero Gemini Quota Â§9** | Stats endpoint must never invoke Gemini API or consume LLM quota. | Stats collection strictly queries memory and local SQLite; zero network calls. | Test verifies Gemini client mock is never called during stats requests. |\n\n---\n\n## 2. Scope Boundaries\n\n### Strictly in Scope for Module 9:\n1. `backend/services/stats_service.py`: Central thread-safe statistics service.\n2. `backend/routes/stats_routes.py`: Dedicated route exposing `GET /api/stats`.\n3. Application registration in `app.py`.\n4. Instrumentation in `chat_routes.py`, `policy_service.py`, and `gemini_service.py`.\n5. Comprehensive test suite in `tests/test_stats_service.py`.\n\n### Explicitly Out of Scope for Module 9:\n1. **Frontend Changes**: Per project roadmap, all frontend interface work (including HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and stats presentation) belongs to **Module 10: Frontend Chat Interface**. No frontend files will be created or modified in Module 9.\n2. **Alternative Endpoints**: `/api/v1/stats` is excluded; only the specified primary endpoint `GET /api/stats` will be implemented.\n3. **Reset Controls**: No public or private reset endpoint (`POST /reset`) will be exposed, preserving security against unauthorized counter manipulation.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Endpoint Contract Specification: `GET /api/stats`\n\n### 3.1 Route Definition\n- **Path:** `/api/stats`\n- **Method:** `GET`\n- **Authentication:** Publicly accessible (contains no sensitive internal state, PII, or tokens).\n- **Allowed Methods:** `GET` only. Requests with `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, etc. return `HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed`.\n\n### 3.2 Response Payload (`HTTP 200 OK`)\nThe endpoint response strictly conforms to Section 9 of the architecture specification:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"total_requests\": 847,\n  \"cache_hits\": 503,\n  \"gemini_calls\": 344,\n  \"errors\": 12,\n  \"uptime_seconds\": 7200,\n  \"worker_note\": \"Counters reflect the current worker process only. Reset on restart.\"\n}\n```\n\n### 3.3 Field Definitions and Types\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| `total_requests` | `int` | Total student chat message requests received at the message endpoint. |\n| `cache_hits` | `int` | Number of requests resolved directly via SQLite cache without calling Gemini. |\n| `gemini_calls` | `int` | Number of actual API calls made to the Google Gemini model. |\n| `errors` | `int` | Cumulative server-side operational and AI generation failures. |\n| `uptime_seconds` | `int` | Seconds elapsed since the worker process started. |\n| `worker_note` | `str` | Exact fixed string: `\"Counters reflect the current worker process only. Reset on restart.\"` |\n\n---\n\n## 4. Metric Definitions and Instrumentation Strategy\n\nTo ensure absolute accuracy without double-counting, each counter is defined with exact trigger conditions and hook locations:\n\n```\n[Incoming Request: POST /api/v1/conversations/{id}/messages]\n       â”‚\n       â–¼\n1. Validate JSON & Conversation Active\n       â”‚\n       â”œâ”€â”€ (Validation fails: HTTP 400/404) â”€â”€> Return Error (Not counted in total_requests)\n       â”‚\n       â–¼\n2. request_mgr.start_request()\n       â”‚\n       â”œâ”€â”€> INCREMENT total_requests (+1)\n       â”‚\n       â”œâ”€â”€ (Duplicate completed replay: HTTP 200) â”€â”€> Return replayed response (No Gemini, No Cache Hit)\n       â”œâ”€â”€ (Rate limited: HTTP 429) â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€> Return 429 (No Gemini, No Cache Hit)\n       â”‚\n       â–¼\n3. policy_service.ask(query)\n       â”‚\n       â”œâ”€â”€ Cache lookup succeeds â”€â”€> INCREMENT cache_hits (+1) â”€â”€> Return answer\n       â”‚\n       â””â”€â”€ Cache miss â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€> Proceed to live retrieval\n                                           â”‚\n                                           â–¼\n                                    gemini_service.generate_text()\n                                           â”‚\n                                           â”œâ”€â”€> INCREMENT gemini_calls (+1)\n                                           â”‚\n                                           â”œâ”€â”€ Gemini succeeds â”€â”€> Cache answer & return\n                                           â”‚\n                                           â””â”€â”€ Gemini throws / fails â”€â”€> INCREMENT errors (+1)\n                                                                       â”€â”€> Return fallback or 500\n```\n\n### 4.1 Detailed Metric Rules\n\n1. **`total_requests`**:\n   - **Definition:** Counts every valid chat message request arriving at `POST /api/v1/conversations/<id>/messages` that passes initial JSON validation and active conversation verification.\n   - **Duplicates:** Included in `total_requests` because a client sent an incoming request, but duplicates do **not** increment `gemini_calls` or `cache_hits`.\n   - **Rate-Limited Requests:** Included in `total_requests` because an incoming request was received and processed by the rate limiter, but does **not** increment `gemini_calls` or `cache_hits`.\n   - **Malformed Requests (HTTP 400 / 404):** Malformed payloads (missing fields, invalid JSON) and requests to nonexistent/deleted conversations are rejected before request processing begins and are not counted as processed chat requests.\n\n2. **`cache_hits`**:\n   - **Definition:** Incremented **only** when `cache_service.get()` returns a valid, unexpired, policy-grounded `CachedAnswer`.\n   - **Exclusions:** Context-dependent queries that bypass cache, cache misses, and expired entries do not increment this counter.\n   - **Instrumentation Hook:** Directly inside `PolicyService.ask()` upon receiving a non-None result from `self.cache_service.get()`.\n\n3. **`gemini_calls`**:\n   - **Definition:** Incremented **only** when an actual network API request to Google Gemini (`generate_text`) is initiated.\n   - **Exclusions:** Never incremented on cache hits, out-of-scope query declines, unsupported topic declines, or extractive fallbacks where the API is not called.\n   - **Instrumentation Hook:** Inside `GeminiService.generate_text()` or immediately prior to the client invocation in `PolicyService`.\n\n4. **`errors`**:\n   - **Definition:** Tracks server-side operational and generation failures during message processing (e.g. Gemini API failure, SQLite operational error, or unhandled exception resulting in HTTP 500/503).\n   - **Exclusions:** Client errors (HTTP 400 Bad Request, HTTP 404 Not Found, HTTP 409 Conflict) and rate limits (HTTP 429) are normal operational rejections, not server errors.\n   - **Double-Counting Prevention:** Captured exclusively in the exception handler or fallback trigger path. Each failed request increments `errors` exactly once.\n\n5. **`uptime_seconds`**:\n   - **Definition:** Calculated as `int(time.time() - self._start_time)` where `_start_time` is recorded using `time.time()` when `StatsService` is instantiated at worker startup.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Verified Database Schema & Aggregation Strategy\n\nWhile the primary contract of `GET /api/stats` requires the 6 in-process metrics above, `StatsService` also provides an internal aggregation utility to verify persistent database health.\n\n### 5.1 Verification of Actual SQLite Schema\nInspection of `backend/services/chat_service.py` and `backend/services/cache_service.py` reveals the exact database structures:\n\n1. **`conversations` Table**:\n   - Columns: `id TEXT PRIMARY KEY`, `created_at TEXT NOT NULL`, `updated_at TEXT NOT NULL`, `status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'`.\n   - **Status Values:**\n     - Active conversations: `status = 'active'`.\n     - Soft-deleted conversations: `status = 'deleted'` (via `update conversations set status = 'deleted'`).\n     - Hard-deleted conversations: row is removed entirely (`DELETE FROM conversations`).\n     - *Conclusion:* A query checking `status = 'active'` is valid; counting total vs. active conversations must account for both soft and hard deletions.\n\n2. **`messages` Table**:\n   - Columns: `id TEXT PRIMARY KEY`, `conversation_id TEXT NOT NULL`, `role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(role IN ('user', 'assistant'))`, `content TEXT NOT NULL`, `created_at TEXT NOT NULL`, `sources TEXT`.\n   - Foreign key references `conversations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`.\n\n3. **`query_cache` Table**:\n   - Columns: `id TEXT PRIMARY KEY`, `cache_key TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL`, `normalized_query TEXT NOT NULL`, `answer TEXT NOT NULL`, `sources TEXT NOT NULL`, `created_at TEXT NOT NULL`, `expires_at TEXT NOT NULL`, `last_accessed_at TEXT NOT NULL`, `access_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1`, etc.\n   - **Timestamp Format:** Stored as UTC ISO 8601 strings (`datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()`, e.g. `'2026-11-11T03:10:45.123456+00:00'`).\n   - *Expiration Comparison:* To compare against `expires_at` accurately in SQLite, the query must pass `datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()` as a parameter (`expires_at > ?`), matching `CacheService.cleanup_expired()`. Do **not** use SQLite's native `datetime('now')` because SQLite uses space separators rather than `'T'`, causing lexicographical comparison discrepancies.\n\n### 5.2 Safe Read-Only Aggregation Query\n```python\ndef get_database_counts(self) -> dict[str, int]:\n    \"\"\"Execute non-blocking read query across SQLite tables using parameter binding.\"\"\"\n    now_iso = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()\n    query = \"\"\"\n        SELECT\n            (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM conversations) AS total_conversations,\n            (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM conversations WHERE status = 'active') AS active_conversations,\n            (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages) AS total_messages,\n            (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM query_cache) AS total_cache_entries,\n            (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM query_cache WHERE expires_at > ?) AS active_cache_entries;\n    \"\"\"\n    # Executed with autocommit connection (isolation_level=None) under WAL mode\n```\n\n---\n\n## 6. In-Memory Counter Design & Thread Safety\n\n### 6.1 Synchronization\nIn Gunicorn running with `--workers 1 --threads 2`, two worker threads process requests concurrently. In Python, operations like `self._total_requests += 1` are not atomic at the bytecode level.\n\nTo guarantee zero race conditions:\n```python\nclass StatsService:\n    def __init__(self, db_path: Optional[str] = None):\n        self._lock = threading.Lock()\n        self._start_time = time.time()\n        self._total_requests = 0\n        self._cache_hits = 0\n        self._gemini_calls = 0\n        self._errors = 0\n        self.db_path = db_path\n\n    def increment_requests(self) -> None:\n        with self._lock:\n            self._total_requests += 1\n\n    def increment_cache_hits(self) -> None:\n        with self._lock:\n            self._cache_hits += 1\n\n    def increment_gemini_calls(self) -> None:\n        with self._lock:\n            self._gemini_calls += 1\n\n    def increment_errors(self) -> None:\n        with self._lock:\n            self._errors += 1\n\n    def get_stats(self) -> dict[str, Any]:\n        with self._lock:\n            total_reqs = self._total_requests\n            hits = self._cache_hits\n            gemini = self._gemini_calls\n            errs = self._errors\n            uptime = int(time.time() - self._start_time)\n\n        return {\n            \"total_requests\": total_reqs,\n            \"cache_hits\": hits,\n            \"gemini_calls\": gemini,\n            \"errors\": errs,\n            \"uptime_seconds\": uptime,\n            \"worker_note\": \"Counters reflect the current worker process only. Reset on restart.\",\n        }\n```\n\n### 6.2 Ephemeral Lifecycle & Single Worker\n- **Scope:** In-process counters reside strictly in the worker's RAM.\n- **Worker Reset:** When the container restarts or redeploys on Render, memory is wiped and counters reset to zero.\n- **Single Worker Alignment:** Because Gunicorn is configured with `--workers 1`, all requests are handled by this single process, eliminating cross-worker count discrepancy.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Security & Information Protection\n\n1. **Strict Field Whitelist:** `GET /api/stats` exposes **only** the 6 mandatory numerical counters and worker note.\n2. **Zero Internal State Leakage:**\n   - No IP addresses or client identifiers.\n   - No session UUIDs or conversation keys.\n   - No prompt texts, question contents, or cached answer snippets.\n   - No API keys or environment secrets.\n3. **No Administrative Controls:**\n   - No `/api/stats/reset` or modification endpoints.\n   - The route accepts `GET` requests only; all other HTTP methods return `405 Method Not Allowed`.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Empirical Performance Verification Plan\n\nRather than making unsubstantiated latency claims, the implementation will measure actual response times empirically:\n\n1. **Benchmark Test (`test_stats_endpoint_latency`):**\n   - Execute 100 sequential requests to `GET /api/stats` using Flask's test client.\n   - Record response times using high-precision `time.perf_counter()`.\n   - Calculate p50, p95, and maximum latency.\n   - Assert that p95 response time is well within an acceptable threshold for an in-memory/WAL read ($< 25\\,\\text{ms}$ in test harness).\n2. **Zero Block on Chat Pipeline:**\n   - Counter increments inside the lock execute $< 1\\,\\mu\\text{s}$, introducing negligible overhead to chat message handling.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Comprehensive Testing Plan\n\nA dedicated test file `tests/test_stats_service.py` will be created with minimum 12 focused tests:\n\n### 9.1 Unit Tests for `StatsService`\n1. `test_stats_initialization`: Verify initial counters are 0, `uptime_seconds >= 0`, and `worker_note` matches specification.\n2. `test_counter_increments`: Verify atomic increments of requests, cache hits, Gemini calls, and errors.\n3. `test_reset_runtime_counters`: Verify reset helper restores counters to 0 (used for test isolation).\n\n### 9.2 Concurrency & Thread-Safety Tests\n4. `test_concurrent_increments`: Launch 20 concurrent threads each performing 100 increments across all counters; assert final values are exactly 2,000 with zero lost updates.\n5. `test_concurrent_reads_during_increments`: Concurrently call `get_stats()` while write threads increment counters, verifying consistent snapshot reads without exceptions.\n\n### 9.3 API Route Tests (`GET /api/stats`)\n6. `test_api_stats_endpoint_schema`: Assert `GET /api/stats` returns `HTTP 200` with the exact 6 keys: `total_requests`, `cache_hits`, `gemini_calls`, `errors`, `uptime_seconds`, `worker_note`.\n7. `test_api_stats_read_only_methods`: Verify `POST /api/stats`, `PUT /api/stats`, and `DELETE /api/stats` return `HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed`.\n8. `test_stats_does_not_call_gemini`: Verify Gemini API client is never called when querying `/api/stats`.\n9. `test_stats_endpoint_latency_benchmark`: Measure 100 iterations of `/api/stats` using `time.perf_counter()` to record empirical p50/p95 response times.\n\n### 9.4 Pipeline Integration Tests\n10. `test_chat_pipeline_increments_total_requests`: Send a message via chat endpoint; verify `total_requests` increments.\n11. `test_cache_hit_increments_cache_hits_only`: Query a cached question; verify `cache_hits` increments while `gemini_calls` does not.\n12. `test_gemini_call_increments_gemini_calls`: Query an uncached question; verify `gemini_calls` increments.\n13. `test_regression_all_modules`: Verify that all 293 existing tests continue to pass with zero regressions.\n\n---\n\n## 10. File-by-File Change Plan\n\n| Action | File Path | Scope & Responsibilities |\n|---|---|---|\n| **CREATE** | `backend/services/stats_service.py` | `StatsService` class with `threading.Lock`, atomic increments, snapshot reading, and singleton accessors (`get_stats_service()`). |\n| **CREATE** | `backend/routes/stats_routes.py` | Flask Blueprint `stats_bp` registering the single primary route `GET /api/stats`. |\n| **MODIFY** | `app.py` | Register `stats_bp` and initialize `app.extensions[\"stats_service\"]`. |\n| **MODIFY** | `backend/routes/chat_routes.py` | Hook `total_requests` on incoming valid messages and errors on unhandled exceptions. |\n| **MODIFY** | `backend/services/policy_service.py` | Hook `cache_hits` on cache hit and `gemini_calls` on model invocation. |\n| **CREATE** | `tests/test_stats_service.py` | 12+ comprehensive unit, concurrency, route schema, and integration tests. |\n| **MODIFY** | `README.md` | Document Module 9 completion, `GET /api/stats` specification, and single-worker reset behavior. |\n\n*Note: Zero frontend files are modified in Module 9.*\n\n---\n\n## 11. Remaining Limitations & Honest Architectural Assessment\n\n1. **Worker-Bound Lifecycle**: Counters are held in memory. Restarting Gunicorn or redeploying the Render service resets all counters to zero. This is a known, accepted trade-off for single-worker in-memory architectures.\n2. **Single-Worker Constraint**: If the application were scaled to multiple Gunicorn workers (`--workers > 1`), in-process counters would represent only the worker handling the request. For multi-worker deployments, a shared store (e.g. Redis) would be required. The current single-worker design (`--workers 1 --threads 2`) makes in-process counters accurate for the whole instance.\n3. **No Historical Rollups**: Counters represent cumulative totals since the last restart. Time-series rollups (e.g. requests per minute over the last 24 hours) are not stored in SQLite to avoid unbounded database growth.\n","Overwrite":true,"Path":"C:\\Users\\ACHYUTHA\\.gemini\\antigravity\\brain\\62506f25-2248-471f-a539-b379d2a489b9\\module9_implementation_plan.md"}}]}

no distributed brokers (e.g. Redis) introduced. | Worker lifecycle documentation and single-process scope verification. |\n| **Persistence Limitations Â§12.3** | Render's ephemeral filesystem wipes on restart; in-process stats reset to zero on worker restart. | Documented restart behavior; uptime measured from process start timestamp. | Service initialization test verifies counters start at zero. |\n| **Zero Gemini Quota Â§9** | Stats endpoint must never invoke Gemini API or consume LLM quota. | Stats collection strictly queries memory and local SQLite; zero network calls. | Test verifies Gemini client mock is never called during stats requests. |\n\n---\n\n## 2. Scope Boundaries\n\n### Strictly in Scope for Module 9:\n1. `backend/services/stats_service.py`: Central thread-safe statistics service.\n2. `backend/routes/stats_routes.py`: Dedicated route exposing `GET /api/stats`.\n3. Application registration in `app.py`.\n4. Instrumentation in `chat_routes.py`, `policy_service.py`, and `gemini_service.py`.\n5. Comprehensive test suite in `tests/test_stats_service.py`.\n\n### Explicitly Out of Scope for Module 9:\n1. **Frontend Changes**: Per project roadmap, all frontend interface work (including HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and stats presentation) belongs to **Module 10: Frontend Chat Interface**. No frontend files will be created or modified in Module 9.\n2. **Alternative Endpoints**: `/api/v1/stats` is excluded; only the specified primary endpoint `GET /api/stats` will be implemented.\n3. **Reset Controls**: No public or private reset endpoint (`POST /reset`) will be exposed, preserving security against unauthorized counter manipulation.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Endpoint Contract Specification: `GET /api/stats`\n\n### 3.1 Route Definition\n- **Path:** `/api/stats`\n- **Method:** `GET`\n- **Authentication:** Publicly accessible (contains no sensitive internal state, PII, or tokens).\n- **Allowed Methods:** `GET` only. Requests with `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, etc. return `HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed`.\n\n### 3.2 Response Payload (`HTTP 200 OK`)\nThe endpoint response strictly conforms to Section 9 of the architecture specification:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"total_requests\": 847,\n  \"cache_hits\": 503,\n  \"gemini_calls\": 344,\n  \"errors\": 12,\n  \"uptime_seconds\": 7200,\n  \"worker_note\": \"Counters reflect the current worker process only. Reset on restart.\"\n}\n```\n\n### 3.3 Field Definitions and Types\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| `total_requests` | `int` | Total student chat message requests received at the message endpoint. |\n| `cache_hits` | `int` | Number of requests resolved directly via SQLite cache without calling Gemini. |\n| `gemini_calls` | `int` | Number of actual API calls made to the Google Gemini model. |\n| `errors` | `int` | Cumulative server-side operational and AI generation failures. |\n| `uptime_seconds` | `int` | Seconds elapsed since the worker process started. |\n| `worker_note` | `str` | Exact fixed string: `\"Counters reflect the current worker process only. Reset on restart.\"` |\n\n---\n\n## 4. Metric Definitions and Instrumentation Strategy\n\nTo ensure absolute accuracy without double-counting, each counter is defined with exact trigger conditions and hook locations:\n\n```\n[Incoming Request: POST /api/v1/conversations/{id}/messages]\n       â”‚\n       â–¼\n1. Validate JSON & Conversation Active\n       â”‚\n       â”œâ”€â”€ (Validation fails: HTTP 400/404) â”€â”€> Return Error (Not counted in total_requests)\n       â”‚\n       â–¼\n2. request_mgr.start_request()\n       â”‚\n       â”œâ”€â”€> INCREMENT total_requests (+1)\n       â”‚\n       â”œâ”€â”€ (Duplicate completed replay: HTTP 200) â”€â”€> Return replayed response (No Gemini, No Cache Hit)\n       â”œâ”€â”€ (Rate limited: HTTP 429) â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€> Return 429 (No Gemini, No Cache Hit)\n       â”‚\n       â–¼\n3. policy_service.ask(query)\n       â”‚\n       â”œâ”€â”€ Cache lookup succeeds â”€â”€> INCREMENT cache_hits (+1) â”€â”€> Return answer\n       â”‚\n       â””â”€â”€ Cache miss â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€> Proceed to live retrieval\n                                           â”‚\n                                           â–¼\n                                    gemini_service.generate_text()\n                                           â”‚\n                                           â”œâ”€â”€> INCREMENT gemini_calls (+1)\n                                           â”‚\n                                           â”œâ”€â”€ Gemini succeeds â”€â”€> Cache answer & return\n                                           â”‚\n                                           â””â”€â”€ Gemini throws / fails â”€â”€> INCREMENT errors (+1)\n                                                                       â”€â”€> Return fallback or 500\n```\n\n### 4.1 Detailed Metric Rules\n\n1. **`total_requests`**:\n   - **Definition:** Counts every valid chat message request arriving at `POST /api/v1/conversations/<id>/messages` that passes initial JSON validation and active conversation verification.\n   - **Duplicates:** Included in `total_requests` because a client sent an incoming request, but duplicates do **not** increment `gemini_calls` or `cache_hits`.\n   - **Rate-Limited Requests:** Included in `total_requests` because an incoming request was received and processed by the rate limiter, but does **not** increment `gemini_calls` or `cache_hits`.\n   - **Malformed Requests (HTTP 400 / 404):** Malformed payloads (missing fields, invalid JSON) and requests to nonexistent/deleted conversations are rejected before request processing begins and are not counted as processed chat requests.\n\n2. **`cache_hits`**:\n   - **Definition:** Incremented **only** when `cache_service.get()` returns a valid, unexpired, policy-grounded `CachedAnswer`.\n   - **Exclusions:** Context-dependent queries that bypass cache, cache misses, and expired entries do not increment this counter.\n   - **Instrumentation Hook:** Directly inside `PolicyService.ask()` upon receiving a non-None result from `self.cache_service.get()`.\n\n3. **`gemini_calls`**:\n   - **Definition:** Incremented **only** when an actual network API request to Google Gemini (`generate_text`) is initiated.\n   - **Exclusions:** Never incremented on cache hits, out-of-scope query declines, unsupported topic declines, or extractive fallbacks where the API is not called.\n   - **Instrumentation Hook:** Inside `GeminiService.generate_text()` or immediately prior to the client invocation in `PolicyService`.\n\n4. **`errors`**:\n   - **Definition:** Tracks server-side operational and generation failures during message processing (e.g. Gemini API failure, SQLite operational error, or unhandled exception resulting in HTTP 500/503).\n   - **Exclusions:** Client errors (HTTP 400 Bad Request, HTTP 404 Not Found, HTTP 409 Conflict) and rate limits (HTTP 429) are normal operational rejections, not server errors.\n   - **Double-Counting Prevention:** Captured exclusively in the exception handler or fallback trigger path. Each failed request increments `errors` exactly once.\n\n5. **`uptime_seconds`**:\n   - **Definition:** Calculated as `int(time.time() - self._start_time)` where `_start_time` is recorded using `time.time()` when `StatsService` is instantiated at worker startup.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Verified Database Schema & Aggregation Strategy\n\nWhile the primary contract of `GET /api/stats` requires the 6 in-process metrics above, `StatsService` also provides an internal aggregation utility to verify persistent database health.\n\n### 5.1 Verification of Actual SQLite Schema\nInspection of `backend/services/chat_service.py` and `backend/services/cache_service.py` reveals the exact database structures:\n\n1. **`conversations` Table**:\n   - Columns: `id TEXT PRIMARY KEY`, `created_at TEXT NOT NULL`, `updated_at TEXT NOT NULL`, `status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'`.\n   - **Status Values:**\n     - Active conversations: `status = 'active'`.\n     - Soft-deleted conversations: `status = 'deleted'` (via `update conversations set status = 'deleted'`).\n     - Hard-deleted conversations: row is removed entirely (`DELETE FROM conversations`).\n     - *Conclusion:* A query checking `status = 'active'` is valid; counting total vs. active conversations must account for both soft and hard deletions.\n\n2. **`messages` Table**:\n   - Columns: `id TEXT PRIMARY KEY`, `conversation_id TEXT NOT NULL`, `role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(role IN ('user', 'assistant'))`, `content TEXT NOT NULL`, `created_at TEXT NOT NULL`, `sources TEXT`.\n   - Foreign key references `conversations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`.\n\n3. **`query_cache` Table**:\n   - Columns: `id TEXT PRIMARY KEY`, `cache_key TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL`, `normalized_query TEXT NOT NULL`, `answer TEXT NOT NULL`, `sources TEXT NOT NULL`, `created_at TEXT NOT NULL`, `expires_at TEXT NOT NULL`, `last_accessed_at TEXT NOT NULL`, `access_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1`, etc.\n   - **Timestamp Format:** Stored as UTC ISO 8601 strings (`datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()`, e.g. `'2026-11-11T03:10:45.123456+00:00'`).\n   - *Expiration Comparison:* To compare against `expires_at` accurately in SQLite, the query must pass `datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()` as a parameter (`expires_at > ?`), matching `CacheService.cleanup_expired()`. Do **not** use SQLite's native `datetime('now')` because SQLite uses space separators rather than `'T'`, causing lexicographical comparison discrepancies.\n\n### 5.2 Safe Read-Only Aggregation Query\n```python\ndef get_database_counts(self) -> dict[str, int]:\n    \"\"\"Execute non-blocking read query across SQLite tables using parameter binding.\"\"\"\n    now_iso = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()\n    query = \"\"\"\n        SELECT\n            (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM conversations) AS total_conversations,\n            (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM conversations WHERE status = 'active') AS active_conversations,\n            (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages) AS total_messages,\n            (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM query_cache) AS total_cache_entries,\n            (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM query_cache WHERE expires_at > ?) AS active_cache_entries;\n    \"\"\"\n    # Executed with autocommit connection (isolation_level=None) under WAL mode\n```\n\n---\n\n## 6. In-Memory Counter Design & Thread Safety\n\n### 6.1 Synchronization\nIn Gunicorn running with `--workers 1 --threads 2`, two worker threads process requests concurrently. In Python, operations like `self._total_requests += 1` are not atomic at the bytecode level.\n\nTo guarantee zero race conditions:\n```python\nclass StatsService:\n    def __init__(self, db_path: Optional[str] = None):\n        self._lock = threading.Lock()\n        self._start_time = time.time()\n        self._total_requests = 0\n        self._cache_hits = 0\n        self._gemini_calls = 0\n        self._errors = 0\n        self.db_path = db_path\n\n    def increment_requests(self) -> None:\n        with self._lock:\n            self._total_requests += 1\n\n    def increment_cache_hits(self) -> None:\n        with self._lock:\n            self._cache_hits += 1\n\n    def increment_gemini_calls(self) -> None:\n        with self._lock:\n            self._gemini_calls += 1\n\n    def increment_errors(self) -> None:\n        with self._lock:\n            self._errors += 1\n\n    def get_stats(self) -> dict[str, Any]:\n        with self._lock:\n            total_reqs = self._total_requests\n            hits = self._cache_hits\n            gemini = self._gemini_calls\n            errs = self._errors\n            uptime = int(time.time() - self._start_time)\n\n        return {\n            \"total_requests\": total_reqs,\n            \"cache_hits\": hits,\n            \"gemini_calls\": gemini,\n            \"errors\": errs,\n            \"uptime_seconds\": uptime,\n            \"worker_note\": \"Counters reflect the current worker process only. Reset on restart.\",\n        }\n```\n\n### 6.2 Ephemeral Lifecycle & Single Worker\n- **Scope:** In-process counters reside strictly in the worker's RAM.\n- **Worker Reset:** When the container restarts or redeploys on Render, memory is wiped and counters reset to zero.\n- **Single Worker Alignment:** Because Gunicorn is configured with `--workers 1`, all requests are handled by this single process, eliminating cross-worker count discrepancy.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Security & Information Protection\n\n1. **Strict Field Whitelist:** `GET /api/stats` exposes **only** the 6 mandatory numerical counters and worker note.\n2. **Zero Internal State Leakage:**\n   - No IP addresses or client identifiers.\n   - No session UUIDs or conversation keys.\n   - No prompt texts, question contents, or cached answer snippets.\n   - No API keys or environment secrets.\n3. **No Administrative Controls:**\n   - No `/api/stats/reset` or modification endpoints.\n   - The route accepts `GET` requests only; all other HTTP methods return `405 Method Not Allowed`.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Empirical Performance Verification Plan\n\nRather than making unsubstantiated latency claims, the implementation will measure actual response times empirically:\n\n1. **Benchmark Test (`test_stats_endpoint_latency`):**\n   - Execute 100 sequential requests to `GET /api/stats` using Flask's test client.\n   - Record response times using high-precision `time.perf_counter()`.\n   - Calculate p50, p95, and maximum latency.\n   - Assert that p95 response time is well within an acceptable threshold for an in-memory/WAL read ($< 25\\,\\text{ms}$ in test harness).\n2. **Zero Block on Chat Pipeline:**\n   - Counter increments inside the lock execute $< 1\\,\\mu\\text{s}$, introducing negligible overhead to chat message handling.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Comprehensive Testing Plan\n\nA dedicated test file `tests/test_stats_service.py` will be created with minimum 12 focused tests:\n\n### 9.1 Unit Tests for `StatsService`\n1. `test_stats_initialization`: Verify initial counters are 0, `uptime_seconds >= 0`, and `worker_note` matches specification.\n2. `test_counter_increments`: Verify atomic increments of requests, cache hits, Gemini calls, and errors.\n3. `test_reset_runtime_counters`: Verify reset helper restores counters to 0 (used for test isolation).\n\n### 9.2 Concurrency & Thread-Safety Tests\n4. `test_concurrent_increments`: Launch 20 concurrent threads each performing 100 increments across all counters; assert final values are exactly 2,000 with zero lost updates.\n5. `test_concurrent_reads_during_increments`: Concurrently call `get_stats()` while write threads increment counters, verifying consistent snapshot reads without exceptions.\n\n### 9.3 API Route Tests (`GET /api/stats`)\n6. `test_api_stats_endpoint_schema`: Assert `GET /api/stats` returns `HTTP 200` with the exact 6 keys: `total_requests`, `cache_hits`, `gemini_calls`, `errors`, `uptime_seconds`, `worker_note`.\n7. `test_api_stats_read_only_methods`: Verify `POST /api/stats`, `PUT /api/stats`, and `DELETE /api/stats` return `HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed`.\n8. `test_stats_does_not_call_gemini`: Verify Gemini API client is never called when querying `/api/stats`.\n9. `test_stats_endpoint_latency_benchmark`: Measure 100 iterations of `/api/stats` using `time.perf_counter()` to record empirical p50/p95 response times.\n\n### 9.4 Pipeline Integration Tests\n10. `test_chat_pipeline_increments_total_requests`: Send a message via chat endpoint; verify `total_requests` increments.\n11. `test_cache_hit_increments_cache_hits_only`: Query a cached question; verify `cache_hits` increments while `gemini_calls` does not.\n12. `test_gemini_call_increments_gemini_calls`: Query an uncached question; verify `gemini_calls` increments.\n13. `test_regression_all_modules`: Verify that all 293 existing tests continue to pass with zero regressions.\n\n---\n\n## 10. File-by-File Change Plan\n\n| Action | File Path | Scope & Responsibilities |\n|---|---|---|\n| **CREATE** | `backend/services/stats_service.py` | `StatsService` class with `threading.Lock`, atomic increments, snapshot reading, and singleton accessors (`get_stats_service()`). |\n| **CREATE** | `backend/routes/stats_routes.py` | Flask Blueprint `stats_bp` registering the single primary route `GET /api/stats`. |\n| **MODIFY** | `app.py` | Register `stats_bp` and initialize `app.extensions[\"stats_service\"]`. |\n| **MODIFY** | `backend/routes/chat_routes.py` | Hook `total_requests` on incoming valid messages and errors on unhandled exceptions. |\n| **MODIFY** | `backend/services/policy_service.py` | Hook `cache_hits` on cache hit and `gemini_calls` on model invocation. |\n| **CREATE** | `tests/test_stats_service.py` | 12+ comprehensive unit, concurrency, route schema, and integration tests. |\n| **MODIFY** | `README.md` | Document Module 9 completion, `GET /api/stats` specification, and single-worker reset behavior. |\n\n*Note: Zero frontend files are modified in Module 9.*\n\n---\n\n## 11. Remaining Limitations & Honest Architectural Assessment\n\n1. **Worker-Bound Lifecycle**: Counters are held in memory. Restarting Gunicorn or redeploying the Render service resets all counters to zero. This is a known, accepted trade-off for single-worker in-memory architectures.\n2. **Single-Worker Constraint**: If the application were scaled to multiple Gunicorn workers (`--workers > 1`), in-process counters would represent only the worker handling the request. For multi-worker deployments, a shared store (e.g. Redis) would be required. The current single-worker design (`--workers 1 --threads 2`) makes in-process counters accurate for the whole instance.\n3. **No Historical Rollups**: Counters represent cumulative totals since the last restart. Time-series rollups (e.g. requests per minute over the last 24 hours) are not stored in SQLite to avoid unbounded database growth.\n","Overwrite":true,"Path":"c:\\Users\\ACHYUTHA\\OneDrive\\Desktop\\API M&H Dashboard\\dpm101-chatbot\\module9_implementation_plan.md"}}]}

Total conversations count uses `COUNT(*)`, while active conversations count uses `SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'active' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)`.\n  - `query_cache`: Expiration timestamps are stored as UTC ISO 8601 strings (`datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()`). The `stats_routes.py` file includes error handling with logging in the event that `StatsService.get_stats()` throws an exception.\n\n\n","tool_calls":[{"name":"write_file","args":{"Content":"\"\"\"\nbackend/services/stats_service.py â€” Thread-Safe Statistics & Live Counters Service\n\nModule 9: Statistics & Live Counters\nMaintains real-time in-process operational metrics for the single Gunicorn worker:\n  - total_requests: chat message requests received\n  - cache_hits: queries served directly from SQLite cache\n  - gemini_calls: actual API invocations to Google Gemini\n  - errors: server-side operational or generation failures\n  - uptime_seconds: elapsed seconds since worker process start\n  - worker_note: disclaimer explaining single-worker scope and restart loss\n\nAll metrics are synchronized via threading.Lock to guarantee thread-safe\natomic updates and consistent snapshot retrieval across concurrent worker threads.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\nimport threading\nimport time\nfrom typing import Optional, Any\nfrom flask import current_app\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\nWORKER_NOTE = \"Counters reflect the current worker process only. Reset on restart.\"\n\n\nclass StatsService:\n    \"\"\"\n    Thread-safe in-process counter service for operational monitoring.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, start_time: Optional[float] = None) -> None:\n        self._lock = threading.Lock()\n        self._start_time = start_time if start_time is not None else time.time()\n        self._total_requests = 0\n        self._cache_hits = 0\n        self._gemini_calls = 0\n        self._errors = 0\n\n    @property\n    def start_time(self) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Process start timestamp.\"\"\"\n        return self._start_time\n\n    def increment_requests(self, count: int = 1) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Increment total_requests atomically.\"\"\"\n        with self._lock:\n            self._total_requests += count\n\n    def increment_cache_hits(self, count: int = 1) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Increment cache_hits atomically.\"\"\"\n        with self._lock:\n            self._cache_hits += count\n\n    def increment_gemini_calls(self, count: int = 1) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Increment gemini_calls atomically.\"\"\"\n        with self._lock:\n            self._gemini_calls += count\n\n    def increment_errors(self, count: int = 1) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Increment errors atomically.\"\"\"\n        with self._lock:\n            self._errors += count\n\n    def get_stats(self) -> dict[str, Any]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Retrieve a thread-safe snapshot of public operational statistics.\n        Returns exactly the 6 fields specified in Architecture Specification Â§9:\n          - total_requests: int\n          - cache_hits: int\n          - gemini_calls: int\n          - errors: int\n          - uptime_seconds: int\n          - worker_note: str\n        \"\"\"\n        with self._lock:\n            uptime = int(time.time() - self._start_time)\n            return {\n                \"total_requests\": self._total_requests,\n                \"cache_hits\": self._cache_hits,\n                \"gemini_calls\": self._gemini_calls,\n                \"errors\": self._errors,\n                \"uptime_seconds\": max(0, uptime),\n                \"worker_note\": WORKER_NOTE,\n            }\n\n    def reset(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"\n        Reset runtime counters to zero (primarily for unit test isolation).\n        Does not alter worker start time.\n        \"\"\"\n        with self._lock:\n            self._total_requests = 0\n            self._cache_hits = 0\n            self._gemini_calls = 0\n            self._errors = 0\n\n\n# Module-level singleton instance\n_stats_service_instance: Optional[StatsService] = None\n\n\ndef get_stats_service() -> StatsService:\n    \"\"\"\n    Retrieve configured StatsService instance.\n    Prefers current_app.extensions[\"stats_service\"] if inside an active Flask app context,\n    otherwise uses the module-level singleton instance.\n    \"\"\"\n    global _stats_service_instance\n    try:\n        if current_app:\n            app_service = current_app.extensions.get(\"stats_service\")\n            if app_service:\n                return app_service\n    except (RuntimeError, AttributeError):\n        pass\n\n    if _stats_service_instance is None:\n        _stats_service_instance = StatsService()\n    return _stats_service_instance\n\n\ndef set_stats_service(service: Optional[StatsService]) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Explicitly inject a StatsService instance (useful for unit test isolation).\"\"\"\n    global _stats_service_instance\n    _stats_service_instance = service\n","Overwrite":true,"Path":"c:\\Users\\ACHYUTHA\\OneDrive\\Desktop\\API M&H Dashboard\\dpm101-chatbot\\backend\\services\\stats_service.py"}}]}

{"step_index":1818,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-11-11T03:15:05Z","input_tokens":2114,"cache_read_tokens":127272,"output_tokens":421,"tool_calls":[{"name":"write_file","args":{"Content":"\"\"\"\nbackend/routes/stats_routes.py â€” Flask Blueprint for Statistics Endpoints\n\nModule 9: Statistics & Live Counters\nExposes:\n  - GET /api/stats -> Public operational statistics\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\nfrom flask import Blueprint, jsonify\nfrom backend.services.stats_service import get_stats_service\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n# Register directly under /api prefix per Architecture Specification Â§9\nstats_bp = Blueprint(\"stats\", __name__, url_prefix=\"/api\")\n\n\n@stats_bp.route(\"/stats\", methods=[\"GET\"])\ndef get_stats():\n    \"\"\"\n    Public statistics and operational counter endpoint.\n    Returns the exact 6 fields specified in Architecture Â§9:\n      - total_requests: int\n      - cache_hits: int\n      - gemini_calls: int\n      - errors: int\n      - uptime_seconds: int\n      - worker_note: str\n\n    Does NOT call the Gemini API, ensuring zero quota consumption.\n    Safe against concurrent read/write execution.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        service = get_stats_service()\n        data = service.get_stats()\n        return jsonify(data), 200\n    except Exception as exc:\n        logger.exception(\"Failed to retrieve statistics: %s\", exc)\n        return jsonify({\n            \"error\": \"Failed to retrieve statistics\",\n            \"code\": \"STATS_UNAVAILABLE\",\n        }), 503\n","Overwrite":true,"Path":"c:\\Users\\ACHYUTHA\\OneDrive\\Desktop\\API M&H Dashboard\\dpm101-chatbot\\backend\\routes\\stats_routes.py"}}]}

== 5\n        assert data[\"errors\"] == 1\n\n    def test_reset_counters(self, clean_stats):\n        \"\"\"Reset must restore all counters to 0 without altering start time.\"\"\"\n        start_time = clean_stats.start_time\n        clean_stats.increment_requests(10)\n        clean_stats.increment_cache_hits(5)\n        clean_stats.increment_gemini_calls(5)\n        clean_stats.increment_errors(2)\n\n        clean_stats.reset()\n        data = clean_stats.get_stats()\n        assert data[\"total_requests\"] == 0\n        assert data[\"cache_hits\"] == 0\n        assert data[\"gemini_calls\"] == 0\n        assert data[\"errors\"] == 0\n        assert clean_stats.start_time == start_time\n\n    def test_uptime_calculation(self):\n        \"\"\"Uptime must accurately reflect elapsed seconds from start_time.\"\"\"\n        fake_start = time.time() - 3600  # 1 hour ago\n        svc = StatsService(start_time=fake_start)\n        data = svc.get_stats()\n        assert data[\"uptime_seconds\"] >= 3600\n        assert data[\"uptime_seconds\"] <= 3605\n\n\n# â”€â”€ 2. Concurrency & Thread-Safety Tests â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€\n\nclass TestStatsServiceConcurrency:\n    def test_concurrent_counter_increments(self, clean_stats):\n        \"\"\"\n        20 concurrent threads each performing 100 increments across all counters.\n        Must result in exactly 2,000 for each counter with zero lost updates.\n        \"\"\"\n        num_threads = 20\n        increments_per_thread = 100\n\n        def worker():\n            for _ in range(increments_per_thread):\n                clean_stats.increment_requests()\n                clean_stats.increment_cache_hits()\n                clean_stats.increment_gemini_calls()\n                clean_stats.increment_errors()\n\n        threads = [threading.Thread(target=worker) for _ in range(num_threads)]\n        for t in threads:\n            t.start()\n        for t in threads:\n            t.join()\n\n        data = clean_stats.get_stats()\n        expected = num_threads * increments_per_thread\n        assert data[\"total_requests\"] == expected\n        assert data[\"cache_hits\"] == expected\n        assert data[\"gemini_calls\"] == expected\n        assert data[\"errors\"] == expected\n\n    def test_concurrent_reads_during_writes(self, clean_stats):\n        \"\"\"\n        Simultaneous read and write threads must execute without deadlock\n        or inconsistent state exceptions.\n        \"\"\"\n        stop_event = threading.Event()\n        read_results = []\n\n        def writer():\n            while not stop_event.is_set():\n                clean_stats.increment_requests()\n                clean_stats.increment_cache_hits()\n                time.sleep(0.001)\n\n        def reader():\n            while not stop_event.is_set():\n                stats = clean_stats.get_stats()\n                read_results.append(stats[\"total_requests\"])\n                time.sleep(0.001)\n\n        writer_thread = threading.Thread(target=writer)\n        reader_thread = threading.Thread(target=reader)\n\n        writer_thread.start()\n        reader_thread.start()\n        time.sleep(0.1)\n        stop_event.set()\n\n        writer_thread.join()\n        reader_thread.join()\n\n        assert len(read_results) > 0\n        assert all(isinstance(r, int) for r in read_results)\n\n\n# â”€â”€ 3. API Route Tests: GET /api/stats â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€\n\nclass TestStatsEndpoint:\n    def test_get_stats_schema_and_status(self, client, clean_stats):\n        \"\"\"GET /api/stats must return HTTP 200 with the exact 6 required fields.\"\"\"\n        clean_stats.increment_requests(10)\n        clean_stats.increment_cache_hits(6)\n        clean_stats.increment_gemini_calls(4)\n        clean_stats.increment_errors(1)\n\n        resp = client.get(\"/api/stats\")\n        assert resp.status_code == 200\n        assert resp.is_json\n\n        data = resp.get_json()\n        assert set(data.keys()) == {\n            \"total_requests\",\n            \"cache_hits\",\n            \"gemini_calls\",\n            \"errors\",\n            \"uptime_seconds\",\n            \"worker_note\",\n        }\n        assert data[\"total_requests\"] == 10\n        assert data[\"cache_hits\"] == 6\n        assert data[\"gemini_calls\"] == 4\n        assert data[\"errors\"] == 1\n        assert isinstance(data[\"uptime_seconds\"], int)\n        assert data[\"worker_note\"] == WORKER_NOTE\n\n    def test_http_method_restrictions(self, client):\n        \"\"\"Endpoints must reject POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH with 405 Method Not Allowed.\"\"\"\n        assert client.post(\"/api/stats\").status_code == 405\n        assert client.put(\"/api/stats\").status_code == 405\n        assert client.delete(\"/api/stats\").status_code == 405\n        assert client.patch(\"/api/stats\").status_code == 405\n\n    def test_stats_does_not_call_gemini(self, client):\n        \"\"\"Querying /api/stats must NEVER invoke Gemini API or consume quota.\"\"\"\n        with patch(\"backend.services.gemini_service.GeminiService.generate_text\") as mock_gemini:\n            resp = client.get(\"/api/stats\")\n            assert resp.status_code == 200\n            mock_gemini.assert_not_called()\n\n    def test_stats_graceful_failure(self, client, test_app):\n        \"\"\"If StatsService raises an unhandled error, endpoint returns HTTP 503.\"\"\"\n        mock_service = MagicMock()\n        mock_service.get_stats.side_effect = RuntimeError(\"Database locked or memory corrupted\")\n        test_app.extensions[\"stats_service\"] = mock_service\n\n        resp = client.get(\"/api/stats\")\n        assert resp.status_code == 503\n        data = resp.get_json()\n        assert data[\"code\"] == \"STATS_UNAVAILABLE\"\n\n\n# â”€â”€ 4. Pipeline Instrumentation & Metric Accuracy Tests â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€\n\nclass TestPipelineInstrumentation:\n    def test_chat_message_increments_total_requests(self, client, clean_stats):\n        \"\"\"Valid chat message must increment total_requests.\"\"\"\n        # 1. Create conversation\n        conv_resp = client.post(\"/api/v1/conversations\")\n        conv_id = conv_resp.get_json()[\"id\"]\n\n        initial_requests = clean_stats.get_stats()[\"total_requests\"]\n\n        # 2. Send message\n        client.post(\n            f\"/api/v1/conversations/{conv_id}/messages\",\n            json={\"message\": \"What is the final exam date?\"},\n        )\n\n        final_requests = clean_stats.get_stats()[\"total_requests\"]\n        assert final_requests == initial_requests + 1\n\n    def test_cache_hit_increments_cache_hits_only(self, clean_stats):\n        \"\"\"A cache hit must increment cache_hits without incrementing gemini_calls.\"\"\"\n        mock_cache = MagicMock()\n        mock_cached_answer = MagicMock()\n        mock_cached_answer.answer = \"The final exam is Nov 20, 2026.\"\n        mock_cached_answer.sources = [\"Doc 04\"]\n        mock_cached_answer.confidence = 1.0\n        mock_cached_answer.model_used = \"gemini-3.8-flash\"\n        mock_cached_answer.prompt_tokens = 10\n        mock_cached_answer.candidates_tokens = 5\n        mock_cached_answer.total_tokens = 15\n        mock_cache.is_enabled.return_value = True\n        mock_cache.get.return_value = mock_cached_answer\n\n        policy_svc = PolicyService(cache_service=mock_cache)\n        ans = policy_svc.ask(\"When is the final exam?\")\n\n        stats = clean_stats.get_stats()\n        assert stats[\"cache_hits\"] == 1\n        assert stats[\"gemini_calls\"] == 0\n        assert ans.answer == \"The final exam is Nov 20, 2026.\"\n\n    def test_gemini_call_increments_gemini_calls_only(self, clean_stats):\n        \"\"\"A cache miss that invokes Gemini must increment gemini_calls and not cache_hits.\"\"\"\n        mock_cache = MagicMock()\n        mock_cache.is_enabled.return_value = True\n        mock_cache.get.return_value = None  # Cache miss\n\n        mock_gemini = MagicMock()\n        mock_gemini.generate_text.return_value = GeminiResponse(\n            success=True,\n            text=\"The passing grade requires 60% overall.\",\n            model=\"gemini-3.8-flash\",\n        )\n\n        policy_svc = PolicyService(gemini_service=mock_gemini, cache_service=mock_cache)\n        policy_svc.ask(\"What is the passing grade?\")\n\n        stats = clean_stats.get_stats()\n        assert stats[\"gemini_calls\"] == 1\n        assert stats[\"cache_hits\"] == 0\n\n    def test_gemini_failure_increments_errors_exactly_once(self, clean_stats):\n        \"\"\"When Gemini fails, errors is incremented exactly once.\"\"\"\n        mock_cache = MagicMock()\n        mock_cache.is_enabled.return_value = True\n        mock_cache.get.return_value = None\n\n        mock_gemini = MagicMock()\n        mock_gemini.generate_text.return_value = GeminiResponse(\n            success=False,\n            error=\"Quota exceeded\",\n            model=\"gemini-3.8-flash\",\n        )\n\n        policy_svc = PolicyService(gemini_service=mock_gemini, cache_service=mock_cache)\n        ans = policy_svc.ask(\"What is the passing grade?\")\n\n        stats = clean_stats.get_stats()\n        assert stats[\"gemini_calls\"] == 1\n        assert stats[\"errors\"] == 1\n        # Fallback answer should still be returned\n        assert ans.answer is not None\n\n    def test_duplicate_request_increments_requests_not_gemini(self, client, clean_stats):\n        \"\"\"Duplicate request replay must increment total_requests but not gemini_calls or cache_hits.\"\"\"\n        conv_resp = client.post(\"/api/v1/conversations\")\n        conv_id = conv_resp.get_json()[\"id\"]\n\n        # First request\n        client.post(\n            f\"/api/v1/conversations/{conv_id}/messages\",\n            json={\"message\": \"What is the certificate fee?\"},\n            headers={\"X-Request-ID\": \"dup-test-uuid-1\"},\n        )\n        stats1 = clean_stats.get_stats()\n        reqs1 = stats1[\"total_requests\"]\n        gemini1 = stats1[\"gemini_calls\"]\n        hits1 = stats1[\"cache_hits\"]\n\n        # Duplicate request with same idempotency key\n        dup_resp = client.post(\n            f\"/api/v1/conversations/{conv_id}/messages\",\n            json={\"message\": \"What is the certificate fee?\"},\n            headers={\"X-Request-ID\": \"dup-test-uuid-1\"},\n        )\n        assert dup_resp.status_code == 200\n        assert dup_resp.headers.get(\"X-Duplicate-Request\") == \"true\"\n\n        stats2 = clean_stats.get_stats()\n        assert stats2[\"total_requests\"] == reqs1 + 1\n        assert stats2[\"gemini_calls\"] == gemini1  # Gemini NOT called on duplicate\n        assert stats2[\"cache_hits\"] == hits1      # Cache NOT called on duplicate\n\n    def test_rate_limited_request_increments_requests_not_gemini(self, client, clean_stats):\n        \"\"\"Rate limited request (429) increments total_requests but not gemini_calls.\"\"\"\n        from backend.services.rate_limiter import SlidingWindowRateLimiter\n        strict_limiter = SlidingWindowRateLimiter(max_requests=1, window_seconds=60)\n        client.application.extensions[\"rate_limiter\"] = strict_limiter\n\n        conv_resp = client.post(\"/api/v1/conversations\")\n        conv_id = conv_resp.get_json()[\"id\"]\n\n        # Request 1: allowed\n        r1 = client.post(f\"/api/v1/conversations/{conv_id}/messages\", json={\"message\": \"Hello 1\"})\n        assert r1.status_code == 200\n\n        stats1 = clean_stats.get_stats()\n        gemini1 = stats1[\"gemini_calls\"]\n\n        # Request 2: rate limited\n        r2 = client.post(f\"/api/v1/conversations/{conv_id}/messages\", json={\"message\": \"Hello 2\"})\n        assert r2.status_code == 429\n\n        stats2 = clean_stats.get_stats()\n        assert stats2[\"total_requests\"] == stats1[\"total_requests\"] + 1\n        assert stats2[\"gemini_calls\"] == gemini1  # Gemini NOT called on rate limited request\n\n\n# â”€â”€ 5. Empirical Latency Benchmark â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€\n\nclass TestStatsLatencyBenchmark:\n    def test_stats_endpoint_latency(self, client):\n        \"\"\"\n        Empirically measure latency of 100 sequential GET /api/stats requests.\n        Calculates min, max, avg, p50, and p95 latency.\n        \"\"\"\n        latencies_ms = []\n        for _ in range(100):\n            t0 = time.perf_counter()\n            resp = client.get(\"/api/stats\")\n            t1 = time.perf_counter()\n            assert resp.status_code == 200\n            latencies_ms.append((t1 - t0) * 1000.0)\n\n        latencies_sorted = sorted(latencies_ms)\n        min_lat = min(latencies_sorted)\n        max_lat = max(latencies_sorted)\n        avg_lat = sum(latencies_sorted) / len(latencies_sorted)\n        p50_lat = latencies_sorted[49]\n        p95_lat = latencies_sorted[94]\n\n        # Log measured performance metrics\n        print(f\"\\n[GET /api/stats Benchmark (100 reqs)] Min: {min_lat:.2f}ms | Avg: {avg_lat:.2f}ms | p50: {p50_lat:.2f}ms | p95: {p95_lat:.2f}ms | Max: {max_lat:.2f}ms\")\n\n        # Sanity assertion for in-memory read inside test harness (< 50ms)\n        assert p95_lat < 50.0, f\"p95 latency was higher than expected: {p95_lat:.2f}ms\"\n","Overwrite":true,"Path":"c:\\Users\\ACHYUTHA\\OneDrive\\Desktop\\API M&H Dashboard\\dpm101-chatbot\\tests\\test_stats_service.py"}}]}

{"step_index":1878,"source":"MODEL","type":"GENERIC","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-11-11T03:20:30Z","content":"Created At: 2026-11-11T08:50:30+05:30\nCompleted At: 2026-11-11T08:50:31+05:30\nShowing lines 330-349 of 349\n330:   - Automatically fingerprints rapid submissions within 10 seconds: `SHA-256(conversation_id + \"::\" + normalized_query)`.\n331:   - Replays completed responses directly from memory with `is_duplicate: true` and `X-Duplicate-Request: true` without inserting redundant database rows.\n332:   - Duplicate retries do not consume rate limit quota.\n333:   - Intentional repeated questions asked after the 10-second deduplication window are processed normally as fresh turns.\n334: - **Turn Serialization & Concurrency Control**:\n335:   - Per-conversation thread locks ensure turns do not interleave within the same conversation.\n336:   - Bounded 5.0-second lock acquisition timeout returns `HTTP 409 Conflict` (`CONVERSATION_BUSY`) rather than blocking indefinitely.\n337:   - In-flight identical requests coordinate using condition variables (`threading.Condition`), eliminating redundant Gemini calls.\n338:   - Independent conversations execute concurrently in parallel.\n339: \n340: ### 2. Operational Security\n341: \n342: - **Safe Proxy Header Inspection**: Uses configured trusted proxy counts (`TRUSTED_PROXIES_COUNT = 1`) to extract authentic client IPs from `X-Forwarded-For` without trusting attacker-spoofed header prefixes.\n343: - **Zero Public Admin Endpoints**: No public administrative reset or internal state dumping endpoints are exposed, preventing rate-limit bypass and information disclosure attacks.\n344: \n345: ---\n346: \n347: ## Next Steps\n348: \n349: Module 9 will implement Statistics & Live Counters."}

{"step_index":1881,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-11-11T03:20:35Z","input_tokens":2335,"cache_read_tokens":152935,"output_tokens":775,"tool_calls":[{"name":"edit_file","args":{"Path":"c:\\Users\\ACHYUTHA\\OneDrive\\Desktop\\API M&H Dashboard\\dpm101-chatbot\\README.md","Replacement":"---\n\n## Module 9: Statistics & Live Counters\n\nModule 9 adds thread-safe in-process counters and a dedicated public statistics endpoint (`GET /api/stats`) providing real-time visibility into system throughput, cache effectiveness, AI generation activity, errors, and process uptime.\n\n### 1. In-Process Counters Architecture (`backend/services/stats_service.py`)\n\n- **Thread-Safe Synchronization**: Uses an instance-level `threading.Lock` to guarantee atomic counter updates and consistent snapshot retrieval across concurrent worker threads (`--workers 1 --threads 2`).\n- **Zero Gemini Quota Consumption**: Fetching statistics operates entirely in-memory, never calling the Gemini API or consuming LLM quota.\n- **Strict Metric Definitions**:\n  - `total_requests`: Counts valid incoming chat message requests received at `POST /api/v1/conversations/{id}/messages`. Includes duplicate replays and rate-limited requests, but excludes malformed inputs (HTTP 400) or nonexistent conversations (HTTP 404).\n  - `cache_hits`: Incremented only when `cache_service.get()` returns a valid, unexpired policy answer.\n  - `gemini_calls`: Incremented only when the Google Gemini API generation is actually invoked.\n  - `errors`: Incremented on server-side operational or generation failures (e.g. Gemini provider failure or unhandled exception). Captured with exactly-once counting per failed request.\n  - `uptime_seconds`: Computed as `int(time.time() - start_time)` from process initialization.\n  - `worker_note`: Required architectural disclaimer: `\"Counters reflect the current worker process only. Reset on restart.\"`\n\n### 2. Operational Statistics API\n\n#### Endpoint\n`GET /api/stats`\n\n#### Response (`HTTP 200 OK`)\n```json\n{\n  \"total_requests\": 847,\n  \"cache_hits\": 503,\n  \"gemini_calls\": 344,\n  \"errors\": 12,\n  \"uptime_seconds\": 7200,\n  \"worker_note\": \"Counters reflect the current worker process only. Reset on restart.\"\n}\n```\n\n#### Security & Access\n- **Read-Only**: Non-GET methods (`POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, `PATCH`) return `HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed`.\n- **Zero Information Leakage**: Exposes only the 6 required numerical counters and the worker disclaimer. Contains no IP addresses, user identifiers, session IDs, request IDs, prompts, or secrets.\n- **No Public Reset Controls**: Does not expose reset endpoints, preventing unauthorized metric manipulation.\n\n### 3. Deployment & Lifecycle Disclosures\n\n- **Single-Worker Scope**: Counters reside in the memory of the single Gunicorn worker process (`--workers 1 --threads 2`). They accurately reflect process-wide metrics without cross-process inconsistency.\n- **Ephemeral Container Restart Loss**: On free-tier cloud platforms like Render, container restarts and redeployments wipe in-memory state. All counters reset to zero upon worker process boot.\n\n---\n\n## Next Steps\n\nModule 10 will implement the Frontend Chat Interface.","Target":"---\n\n## Next Steps\n\nModule 9 will implement Statistics & Live Counters."}}]}

Executive Summary\n\nModule 9 successfully delivers the **Statistics & Live Counters** subsystem for the DPM-101 Course Helpdesk Chatbot. The implementation strictly adheres to the approved `module9_implementation_plan.md` (Phase 1B), providing thread-safe in-process metrics, accurate pipeline instrumentation, and the public read-only endpoint `GET /api/stats`.\n\n### Key Deliverables Completed\n1. **Thread-Safe In-Process Counter Service (`backend/services/stats_service.py`)**:\n   - Maintains real-time accumulators for `total_requests`, `cache_hits`, `gemini_calls`, `errors`, and `uptime_seconds`.\n   - Uses an instance-level `threading.Lock` guaranteeing thread safety under multi-threaded Gunicorn execution (`--workers 1 --threads 2`).\n   - Zero quota consumption: Operates completely in-memory without invoking Gemini or querying external networks.\n2. **Dedicated Operational API (`backend/routes/stats_routes.py`)**:\n   - Exposes `GET /api/stats` directly returning the exact 6 fields specified in Architecture Â§9.\n   - Enforces read-only HTTP method restrictions (`405 Method Not Allowed` for `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, `PATCH`).\n   - Exposes zero sensitive data: No IP addresses, request IDs, session tokens, prompts, or database internals.\n3. **Pipeline Instrumentation**:\n   - `backend/routes/chat_routes.py`: Instruments `total_requests` at the valid message processing boundary; instruments `errors` on unhandled server-side exceptions.\n   - `backend/services/policy_service.py`: Instruments `cache_hits` strictly on valid cache hits; instruments `gemini_calls` strictly when the model API call begins; instruments `errors` on model provider failure.\n4. **Empirical Performance Benchmark**:\n   - 100 sequential requests to `GET /api/stats` measured via `time.perf_counter()`.\n   - Measured results: **Min: 0.18 ms | Avg: 0.24 ms | p50: 0.19 ms | p95: 0.32 ms | Max: 3.14 ms**.\n5. **Full Regression Preservation**:\n   - All 293 previously approved regression tests pass.\n   - 17 new comprehensive Module 9 tests pass.\n   - Total test suite: **310 / 310 passed** with zero regressions.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Implemented & Modified Files\n\n### A. Created Files\n| File Path | Description | Lines of Code |\n|---|---|---|\n| `backend/services/stats_service.py` | `StatsService` class with `threading.Lock`, atomic increments, snapshot retrieval, and singleton accessors (`get_stats_service()`). | 125 |\n| `backend/routes/stats_routes.py` | Flask Blueprint `stats_bp` registering the read-only endpoint `GET /api/stats`. | 45 |\n| `tests/test_stats_service.py` | 17 comprehensive unit, concurrency, route, instrumentation, and benchmark tests. | 385 |\n\n### B. Modified Files\n| File Path | Modifications Made |\n|---|---|\n| `app.py` | Registered `stats_bp` blueprint; initialized `app.extensions[\"stats_service\"]` with factory override support. |\n| `backend/routes/chat_routes.py` | Hooked `total_requests` increment on valid message arrival; hooked `errors` increment on unhandled 500 exceptions. |\n| `backend/services/policy_service.py` | Hooked `cache_hits` on cache hit; hooked `gemini_calls` before model text generation; hooked `errors` on Gemini failure. |\n| `README.md` | Updated roadmap to mark Module 9 complete; documented `GET /api/stats` endpoint and worker restart behavior. |\n\n---\n\n## 3. Counter Instrumentation Locations & Trigger Logic\n\n```\nIncoming Request: POST /api/v1/conversations/{id}/messages\nâ”‚\nâ”œâ”€â”€ Step 1: Input & Conversation Active Validation\nâ”‚     â””â”€â”€ If invalid (400/404) â”€â”€> Return client error (Not counted in total_requests)\nâ”‚\nâ”œâ”€â”€ Step 2: request_mgr.start_request()\nâ”‚     â””â”€â”€ [TRIGGER] get_stats_service().increment_requests()  <-- Counted in total_requests\nâ”‚\nâ”œâ”€â”€ Step 3: Duplicate & Rate Limiting Checks\nâ”‚     â”œâ”€â”€ If duplicate replay (200) â”€â”€> Replay from memory (Gemini & Cache NOT invoked)\nâ”‚     â””â”€â”€ If rate limited (429)     â”€â”€> Return 429 (Gemini & Cache NOT invoked)\nâ”‚\nâ”œâ”€â”€ Step 4: Policy Pipeline: policy_service.ask()\nâ”‚     â”œâ”€â”€ Cache Lookup: cache_service.get(query)\nâ”‚     â”‚     â””â”€â”€ If valid cached answer found:\nâ”‚     â”‚           â””â”€â”€ [TRIGGER] get_stats_service().increment_cache_hits()\nâ”‚
